newsitem.title: UK: MARK/MARKKA JUMPS ON FINNISH EMU CONVERSION REMARK.
newsitem.headline: MARK/MARKKA JUMPS ON FINNISH EMU CONVERSION REMARK.

text.p: The mark shot up against the markka, given impetus by Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's comment the markka's central rate in the European exchange rate mechanism would be the right level at which to enter European monetary union.

Niinisto's comment slammed the markka, whose ERM central parity rate is 3.0400 to the mark, down to a session low of 2.9915 per mark compared with 2.9778 in late European trade on Wednesday. It was trading at 2.9900/30 at 1340 GMT.
"The comment is entirely what's caused it (mark/markka's rise) this afternoon...although it doesn't necessarily mean that's what is going to happen," said a trader at a Scandinavian bank in London.
"It does make sense...If you go into any linkage with your currency undervalued it has potential good effects, so Finland would probably be more than happy to go in at 3.04," he said.
Niinisto also said the principles guiding the conversion of national currencies into Europe's single euro currency should be decided as early as possible.
His comments took the mark/markka rate to its highest since June 25.
"The markka had been strengthening recently, partially on Finnish interest rate expectations," said Stephanie Pfeifer, European economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"Considering the economic fundamentals I do think Finland needs higher interest rates. But if they're talking about conversion rates the markka could start moving slowly towards the 3.04 level," she said.
Some said the markka's reaction to Niinisto's comments appeared to be a bit excessive.

"It's pretty obvious that the ERM central rates would be chosen as the conversion rates, so it couldn't have been that much of a surprise to the market," said Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe. "The only currency that would have a real problem with it is the Irish punt."
The punt, which is the strongest currency against the mark in the ERM grouping, also slid this afternoon. The markka currently ranks second in strength in the ERM grid.
The punt fell as low as 2.6753 marks this afternoon compared with its late Wednesday European level of 2.6975. It had recovered slightly to 2.6795/70 by late afternoon.

However, traders attributed the punt's slide mostly to the fall in sterling. The pound had plunged against the mark today following the Bank of England's comment, which followed a 25 basis-point hike in the base rate to 7.00 percent, that interest rates had reached a level consistent with inflation targets.
The mark crosses, however, ignored sterling's slide of more than six pfennigs against the mark and were mostly steady.
The mark was at 3.3734/36 French francs against 3.3745 in late Wednesday trade, and at 977.30/60 lire against 978.05.

Early in the day, the mark had firmed on the crosses on speculation that the German Bundesbank could make an announcement regarding next week's securities repurchase tender, reviving expectations that the central bank could change its repo policy to enable money market rates to drift higher.
The rise was brief, however, as the Bundesbank soon quashed the rumour by saying it was not planning any statement or news conference today.
